translations.text: The Book of Ezra the Scribe, who is called Shealtiel.
In the thirtieth year after the fall of our city, I, Shealtiel, who am Ezra, was in Babylon. I was lying on my bed, troubled, and thoughts were rising in my heart,
because I saw the desolation of Zion and the prosperity of the inhabitants of Babylon.
My spirit was greatly astonished, and I began to speak forceful words to the Most High.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, was it not you who spoke at the beginning, when you formed the earth—and did this by yourself alone—and commanded the dust,
and it gave you Adam as a lifeless body? He was the work of your hands. You breathed the spirit of life into him, and he became alive before you.
You brought him into the paradise that your right hand had planted before the earth came into being.
You gave him a commandment, but he transgressed it. Immediately you decreed death for him and his descendants. From him were born peoples and tribes, languages, nations, and countless families.
Every people went on with their own deeds, acting wickedly and unjustly before you, and you did not restrain them.
Then, in time, you brought a flood upon the earth and upon the inhabitants of the world, and you destroyed them.
Their destruction came all at once. Just as death came to Adam, so death through the flood came to them.
But you left one of them alive with his household, and all the righteous descended from him.
When the inhabitants of the earth began to multiply, they produced many children, peoples, and great multitudes, and again began to act more wickedly than those before them.
And when they acted wickedly before you, you chose for yourself one of them whose name was Abraham.
You loved him and showed him the end of the ages, to him alone, privately between you and him, at night.
You established everlasting covenants with him and told him that you would never abandon his descendants. You gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau.
You chose Jacob as your own inheritance, but you hated Esau, and Jacob became a great people.
When you brought his descendants up from Egypt, you established everlasting covenants with him and brought them to Mount Sinai.
You bent down the heavens and shook the earth. You made the world tremble, caused the depths to quake, and threw the worlds into turmoil.
Your glory passed through four gates—of fire, earthquake, wind, and frost—to give the law to Jacob’s descendants and commandments to the people of Israel.
Yet you did not remove the evil heart from them so that your law might bear fruit among them.
For the first Adam clothed himself with an evil heart, transgressed, and was overcome—and so were all those born from him.
Suffering remained in them, and the law remained in the people’s heart together with the evil root. Then goodness departed and evil came.
Times passed and seasons came to an end. Then you raised up for yourself a servant whose name was David.
You told him to build a city for your name and a house in which offerings from what belongs to you would be presented to you.
This continued for many years, and the inhabitants of the city sinned against you.
They did nothing different from what Adam and all his descendants had done, for they too were clothed with an evil heart.
You handed your city over to your enemies.
Then I said in my heart, “Perhaps the inhabitants of Babylon are doing what is right, and that is why you abandoned Zion.”
When I came here, I saw countless acts of wickedness, and in this thirtieth year I myself saw many injustices. My heart was shaken
when I saw how you tolerate sinners and spare the wicked, while you have destroyed your people and preserved your enemies.
You have not made known to anyone how your way can be understood. Has Babylon acted better than Zion?
Or have you known another people better than Israel? Or what tribe has been as faithful to your covenant as Jacob?
Yet their reward has not appeared, and their labor has borne no fruit. For I have traveled among the nations and seen that they prosper now, although they do not remember your commandments.
Now weigh in the balance our wrongdoing and that of the inhabitants of the world, and let the movement of the beam be seen: [?] it tilts.
Or when have the inhabitants of the world not sinned before you? Or what people has kept your commandments so well?
You can find individuals by name who have kept your commandments, but you cannot find a whole people.
The angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered
and said to me, “Your heart has been greatly shaken by this world, yet you have wanted to understand the way of the Most High.”
I answered, “Yes, my lord.” Again he answered me, “I have been sent to show you three ways and to set three examples before you.
If you can explain one of them to me, I too will show you the way you long to see, and I will teach you why the heart is evil.”
I answered, “Speak, my lord.” He answered me, “Go and weigh out a weight of fire for me, or measure out a measure of wind for me, or call back for me the day that has passed.”
I said to him, “Who among those born can do the things you have said, that you should ask all these things of me, my lord?”

And he said to me, “Suppose I asked you, ‘How many treasuries are there in the heart of the sea? How many springs are there at the surface of the deep? How many paths are there above the firmament? What are the exits from Sheol? What are the paths of Paradise?’”
“You would say to me, ‘I have not gone down into the abyss, nor have I yet gone down into Sheol, nor have I ever ascended to heaven.’
But now I have not asked you about these things, only about fire, wind, and the day—things you have experienced and without which you cannot exist. Yet you have told me nothing about them.”
He said to me, “You cannot understand the things that have grown up with you.

How, then, can your vessel grasp the way of the Most High? For the way of the Most High was created in what cannot be comprehended, and one who is perishable in a perishable world cannot understand the way of the one who is imperishable.” When I heard these things, I fell on my face
and said to him, “It would have been better for us not to have come into existence than to have come and live in wickedness, suffering without knowing why we suffer.”
He answered me, “The forests of trees on the plain went out and devised a plan.
They said, ‘Come, let us go and wage war against the sea, so that it will retreat before us and we can make another forest for ourselves.’
Likewise, the waves of the sea devised a plan and said, ‘Come, let us go up and wage war against the forest of the plain, so that we can make another place for ourselves there too.’
But the forest’s plan came to nothing, for fire came and consumed it.
Likewise, the plan of the waves of the sea came to nothing, for the sand stood firm and restrained them.
If, then, you were their judge, which of them would you acquit, and which would you condemn?”
I answered and said, “Both of them devised a foolish plan. For the land was given to the forest, and the sea its place to carry its waves.”
He answered and said to me, “You have judged well. Why, then, have you not judged yourself?”

“For just as the land is given to the forest, and the sea its place to carry its waves, so those who live on earth can know only what is on earth, and whoever is above heaven can know what is above heaven.”
I answered and said, “I ask you, my lord: why, my lord, was I given understanding with which to think?”

“For I did not wish to ask about the ways above, but about the things that happen to us every day: why Israel has been handed over to the nations, and the people you loved have been handed over to wicked tribes, and the holy law of our ancestors has been abolished, and the written covenants no longer exist.”
“We pass from the world like locusts, and our lives are like a breath. We are not even worthy of being shown mercy.”
“But what will he do for his great name, which has been invoked over us? These are the things I asked about.”
He answered and said to me, “If you live, you will see; and if you live long, you will marvel, because the world is hurrying to pass away.”
“For it cannot bear what has been promised to the righteous, because this world is full of groaning and many illnesses.”
“For the evil you asked me about has been sown, but its harvest has not yet come.”
“So unless what has been sown is harvested, and the place where evil was sown passes away, the land where good has been sown will not come.”
“For a single grain of evil seed was sown in Adam’s heart from the beginning. How much fruit of wickedness it has produced until now! And it will continue to produce until the harvest comes.”
“Consider this for yourself, then, and see how much fruit of wickedness a single grain of evil seed that was sown has produced.”
“When, then, the countless ears of good grain are sown, what a harvest they will produce!”
I answered and said, “How long, and when will these things happen? For our years are few and evil.”
He answered and said to me, “You are not in a greater hurry than the Most High. You are in a hurry for your own sake, but the Most High for the sake of many.”
For the souls of the righteous in their treasuries were not asking about these things. They were saying, “How long are we to remain here? And when will the harvest of our reward come?”
The angel Ramiel answered and said to them, “Until the number of those like you is complete. For the Holy One has weighed the world.”
“He has measured the times and counted the seasons, and he will neither rest nor stir until the appointed number is complete.”
I answered and said, “O Lord, my lord, but look: we are all full of wickedness.”
“Could it be that the reward of the righteous will be held back because of us, because of the sins of those who inhabit the earth?”
He answered and said to me, “Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when her nine months are complete, her womb can still keep the baby inside her.”
I said, “It cannot, my lord.” He answered and said to me, “Sheol and the storehouses of souls are like a womb.”
“For just as a woman giving birth is eager to escape the distress of childbirth, so these too are eager to give up what was placed in them from the beginning.”
“Then the things you long to see will be revealed to you.”
I answered and said, “If I have found mercy in your eyes, and if I am able and worthy—”
Tell me this too: is the time that has passed over us greater, or the time that is yet to come?
For I know the time that has passed, but I do not know what is yet to come.
He answered me, “Stand on the right side, and I will show you the meaning of the parable.”
I stood and looked, and there before me a burning furnace passed by. When the flame had passed, I looked, and there was smoke remaining.
After this, a cloud full of water passed before me and poured down a very heavy rainstorm. When the storm had passed, drops remained in it.

He answered me, “Consider this for yourself and see: just as the rain is greater than the drops, and the fire than the smoke, so the measure of time that has passed was greater. But drops and smoke remain.”
I asked him, “Will I live until those days? Or who will be there in those days?”
He answered me, “As for the signs you asked me about, I can tell you some of them. But I was not sent to tell you about your life, for I do not know either.
“As for the signs, look, days are coming when the inhabitants of the world will be seized with great bewilderment. The portion of truth will be hidden, and the land of faith will become barren.
“Injustice and lawlessness will increase beyond what you have now seen and beyond what you heard long ago.
“This land that you have seen ruling now will have no stability and will not be trodden, and people will see this land lying desolate.
“But if the Most High grants you a vision, you will see what is thrown into turmoil after the third [?]. Suddenly the sun will appear at night, and the moon during the day.
“Wood will drip blood, stone will raise its voice, nations will be shaken, and the winds will change.
“Someone whom many do not expect will reign, and the birds will migrate.
“The Sea of Sodom will produce many fish. Someone unknown to many will raise his voice at night, and everyone will hear it.

“Chasms will open in many places, and fire will repeatedly be sent out. Wild animals will leave their places, and signs will appear through women, for babies will be born before they are fully developed.
Salt water will be found in fresh water. Friends will suddenly wage war against their friends. Then wisdom will be hidden, and understanding will withdraw into its treasuries.
“It will be sought among many but will not be found. Oppression and lawlessness will increase on the earth.
“One region will ask its neighbor, ‘Has righteousness passed through you, or anyone who practices righteousness?’ But that region will deny it.
“At that time people will hope but will not receive; they will toil but will not find; they will labor, but their way will not prosper.
“These are the signs I was commanded to tell you. But if you pray again and seek as you are doing now, and fast for seven days, you will hear things greater than these.”
And I awoke. My body was trembling violently, and my soul was so exhausted that it seemed about to depart.
The angel who was speaking to me took hold of me, strengthened me, and set me on my feet.
On the second night, Phaltiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said, “Where have you been, and why is your face so gloomy?
“Do you not know that you are the one entrusted with Israel in the place of their captivity?
“Get up, then, and eat a little bread, so that you do not abandon them as a shepherd leaves his flock in the clutches of ravenous wolves.”
I said to him, “Go away from me, and do not come near me for seven days. Then come to me, and I will tell you something.” When I had said this to him, he went away from me.
And I fasted for seven days, sighing and weeping, as the angel Ramiel had commanded me.
After seven days, the thoughts of my heart again began to distress me greatly.
My soul received a spirit of understanding, and I again began to speak these words of prayer and supplication before the Most High.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, from all the forests of the earth and its trees you chose one vine for yourself.
And from all the lands of the world you chose one place for yourself.

And from all the depths of the sea you made one stream great for yourself. And from all the flowers of the world you chose one flower for yourself. And from all the cities that have been built you consecrated Zion for yourself.
And from all the birds that were created you designated one dove for yourself. And from all the sheep that were created you took pleasure in one ewe.
And from the multitude of nations you brought one people close to yourself. And you gave the law, chosen above all others, to the people whom you loved.
And now, Lord, why have you handed the one over to the many, and despised the one root more than the many? You have scattered and dispersed your only one among the many.
And those who oppose your commandments have trampled on those who trusted in your covenant.”
But if you truly hated your people, they should have been disciplined by your own hands.
After I had spoken these words, the angel who had been sent to me the previous night was sent to me again.
And he said to me, “Listen to me, Ezra, and I will instruct you. Look at me, and I will set words before you.”
And I answered him, “Speak, my lord.” And he said to me, “You have been deeply troubled over Israel. Or have you loved him more than his Maker?”

And I said, “No, my lord. But I was in great pain, and I spoke, because my innermost being torments me continually. I want to grasp the decree of the Most High and investigate something of his judgment.”

And he said to me, “You cannot.” And I said to him, “Why do I pray, my lord? Or why was I born? Why was my mother’s womb not my grave, so that I would not see Jacob’s suffering and the hardship of Israel’s descendants?”
And he answered me, “Count for me those who have not yet come, and gather for me the drops that have been scattered, and make the withered flowers flourish.

Open for me the storehouses that are locked, and bring out for me the winds confined in them. Show me the likeness of faces that you have not yet seen, or show me the likeness of a voice. Then I will tell you about the suffering and the time that you have sought to see.”
And I said, “O Lord, my Lord, who can know these things except someone who does not dwell among human beings?
But I am foolish and wretched. How can I speak about the things you have asked me?”
And he said to me, “Just as you cannot do one of these things that have been mentioned, so you cannot discover my judgment or the fulfillment of the love that I promised my people.”
And I said, “But, my lord, you have made a promise to those who are at the end. What will those before us do, or we ourselves, or those after us?”
And he answered me, “As for the crown of my coming judgment, just as there is no delay for those who come last, so there is no advance for those who come first.”
And I answered, “Could you not have made those who have been, those who are, and those who will be all at once, so that you might make your judgment known quickly?”
And he answered me, “Creation is not in greater haste than its Creator. Otherwise, the world could not have borne all those who would have come into being in it at once.”

And again I answered, “How, then, did you tell your servant that you would surely bring to life the creation that you created all at once? If, then, they will all live at once and creation will bear them, it could also have borne now those who came into being all at once.”
And he answered me, “Ask a woman’s womb and say to it, ‘If you bear ten children, why do you bear them at separate times?’ Ask it, then, to deliver all ten of them.”
And I said, “She cannot, my lord, except at intervals.”
And he said to me, “I too have made the earth a womb for those who come upon it at intervals.
For just as a little girl cannot give birth, nor can a woman who has grown old, so I too have ordered the world that I created.”

And I asked him, saying, “Now that you have given me an opportunity, I will speak before you. Our mother Zion, about whom you spoke to me—yes, my lord—is she still young, or is she already approaching old age?”
And he answered me, “Ask a woman who gives birth, and she will tell you.
Say to her, ‘Why do those whom you bear now resemble the earlier ones, but are smaller in stature?’
She too will tell you, ‘Those born in the strength of youth are different from those born in old age, when the womb has weakened.’
Look for yourself and see that you are smaller in stature than those who came before you.
Those who come after you will be even smaller than you, because creation has already grown old, and the vigor of its youth has passed away.”
And I answered, “I beg you, my lord, if I have found favor before you, tell your servant through whom you will attend to your creation.”

And he answered me, “At first, through a human being; but the end is in my own hands. For before the earth of the inhabited world existed, before the world's outlets were established, and before the masses of wind began to blow,
before the sound of thunder was heard, before the flashes of lightning shone, and before the ground of paradise was established,
before the beauty of flowers appeared, before the force of earthquakes gained strength, and before the countless armies of angels were gathered,
before the heights of the air were raised, before the expanses of the heavens were named, and before Zion's footstool was established,
before these present years were reckoned, before the offenses of today's sinners were formed, and before those who stored up treasures of faith for themselves were sealed,
then I planned these things, and they all came into being through my hands alone, and not through the hands of another.”
And I answered, “What divides the times? When is the end of the first age, and what marks the beginning of the second?”
And he answered me, “From Abraham to Abraham. Isaac was born to Abraham, and Jacob and Esau were born to Isaac, and Jacob's hand was holding Esau's heel.
The heel belongs to the first, Esau, and the hand to the second, Jacob.
For a person's beginning is his hand, and a person's end is his heel. Therefore, Ezra, do not look for anything else between the heel and the hand.”
And I answered, “O Lord, my lord, if I have found favor in your eyes,
make known to me, your servant, the final outcome of these signs, about which you told me a little last night.”
And he answered me, “Stand on your feet, and you will hear a loud voice.
And if the place where you are standing should shake violently
while you are being addressed, do not be alarmed, because the message concerns the good that comes at the end, and the foundations of the earth will understand.”
The word concerns them, and they are alarmed and shaken, for they perceive that their end is changing.
When I heard this, I stood on my feet. I listened, and there was a voice speaking, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.
He said, “Look, the days are coming, and when I draw near to visit the inhabitants of the earth,
and when I am about to call the wicked to account for what their hands have done, and when Zion’s humiliation comes to an end,
and when this world, which is destined to pass away, is about to be sealed, I will perform these signs: books will be opened across the sky, and everyone will see my judgment together.
One-year-old children will speak and raise their voices. Pregnant women will give birth before their time, to children at three or four months, and they will live and leap about.
Suddenly, places that have not been sown will be found sown, and storehouses that are full will suddenly be found empty.
A horn will sound loudly, and everyone will suddenly hear it and be terrified.
At that time friends will fight against their friends like enemies, and the earth and its inhabitants will be astonished. The outlets of springs will stop flowing for three hours.
Whoever survives all these things that I have told you beforehand will live and see my salvation and the end of the world.
Then he will see those people who were taken up, who have not tasted death since their birth. The hearts of the earth’s inhabitants will be transformed and changed to a different understanding.
For evil will be forgotten, and deceit will be extinguished.
Faithfulness will flourish, corruption will be overcome, and truth, which remained without fruit for many years, will appear.”
While he was speaking with me, the place where I was standing began to shake little by little.
And he said to me, “These are the things I have come to make known to you tonight.”
“If, then, you seek again and fast for seven days, I will reveal to you still greater things than these.
For your voice has indeed been heard by the Most High. The Mighty One has seen your purity, as well as the holiness you have had since your youth.
For this reason he sent me to reveal all these things to you.” And he said to me, “Take courage and do not be afraid.
Do not be hasty in dwelling on the evil times of the past, so that punishment may not come upon you in the last times.”
After these things, I wept and fasted for seven days, to complete the three weeks that had been prescribed for me.
On the eighth night, my heart was again troubled within me, and I began to speak before the Most High,
because my spirit was seething intensely, and my soul was aflame.
I said, “O Lord, my Lord, you spoke at the beginning of your creation, on the first day, and said that heaven and earth should come into being. Your word, my Lord, accomplished the work.
Then the spirit was hovering, darkness covered everything, and there was silence without a sound. There was not yet any human voice.
Then you said that a radiance of light should come out of your own treasuries, so that your works might be seen.
On the second day, you created the spirit of the firmament and commanded it to make a division between the waters, so that one portion of them would rise above and another portion would remain below.
On the third day you commanded the waters to gather into one of the earth’s seven parts. You dried out and preserved six parts, so that they might serve you and be cultivated and sown.
Your own word went out, and immediately the work was done.

For then, suddenly, countless fruits sprang up, sweet to the taste, of every kind; flowers unlike one another in appearance; trees incomparable in their beauty; and aromatic plants whose fragrances were beyond understanding. These things came into being on the third day.
On the fourth day you commanded, and there came into being the shining sun, the radiance of the moon, and the ordered array of stars.
You commanded them to serve the human being who was to be formed by you.
On the fifth day you told the seventh portion, where the waters were, to bring forth living creatures, birds, and fish.
And the waters, which neither spoke nor had life, were producing living things, so that through these, generations might recount your wonders.
Then you kept two living creatures that you had created. You called one Behemoth, and you called the other Leviathan.
You separated them from one another, because that seventh portion, the watery one, could not contain them.
You gave Behemoth one of the portions that you had made dry on the third day, to live there, where there are a thousand mountains.
But to Leviathan you gave one of the seven portions of water. You kept them to be food for whomever you wish, whenever you wish.
On the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you livestock, wild animals, and creeping creatures.
Over these you appointed Adam as ruler over all the works you had created before. From him we come, the people you chose.
I have said all these things before you, O Lord my Lord, because you said that you created this world for our sake.
But as for the rest of the nations descended from Adam, you said that they are nothing. You compared them to spit, and you likened their abundance to a drop from a bucket.
And now, Lord, look: those nations that were counted as nothing rule over us and trample us.
But we, your people whom you honored and called your firstborn, your only one, close and beloved, have been handed over into their hands.
If the world was created for our sake, why do we not inherit our world? How long will these things continue?
After I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the previous nights was sent to me.
He said to me, “Stand up, Ezra, and listen to the words I have come to tell you.”
I said to him, “Speak, my lord.” He answered me, “Suppose a sea lies in a spacious place, so that it is broad and boundless,
but its entrance lies in a narrow place, so that it resembles a river.
If someone wishes to enter the sea, see it, and become its master, how can he reach the spacious place unless he passes through the narrow passage?
Listen to another example. There is a city built and situated on a broad plain, and that city is full of many good things.
Its entrance is narrow and set on a height, with fire on the right and deep water on the left.
A single path lies between the two, between the fire and the water, and that path is only wide enough for a person's foot.
If that city is given as an inheritance, how can the heir take possession of his inheritance unless he passes through the danger that lies before him?”
I said to him, “Yes, that is so, my lord.” He answered me, “So it is also with Israel's portion.”
For I made the world for their sake, and when Adam transgressed my commandments, what had been made was condemned.
Because of this, the entrances to this present world became narrow, full of groaning, toil, great danger, and great weariness, along with sicknesses and sufferings.
But the entrances to the world to come are spacious and free from anxiety, and they bear fruit that does not perish.
Therefore, unless the living pass through these afflictions and evils, they cannot obtain the things laid up for them.
Why, then, are you now troubled, since you are perishable? And why are you distressed, since you are mortal?
And why have you not taken to heart what is to come, but only what is present?
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, you have clearly stated in your law that the righteous will inherit these things, but the wicked will perish.
“The righteous, then, willingly endure afflictions because they hope to come to a place of relief. But the wicked bear afflictions and will see no relief.”
And he answered me, “You are not wiser than God, nor do you have greater understanding than the Most High.”
“Therefore many who have come into being will perish, because they have despised the law established by me.
“For when they came into being, God commanded those who came into being what they should do to live, and what they should observe to avoid punishment.
“But they rebelled and did not obey him, and devised empty thoughts for themselves.
“They also developed schemes that lead to ruin, and on top of all this they said that the Most High does not exist, and they did not acknowledge his ways.
“They scorned his law, denied his covenants, did not believe his commandments, and despised his works.
“Therefore, Ezra, empty things are for the empty, and full things for those who are full.
“For look, the days are coming, and when the signs I told you about earlier come, the bride who appears as a city will be revealed, and she who is now set apart will be seen.
“Everyone who escapes these evils foretold long ago will see my wonders.
“For my son, the Messiah, will be revealed with those who are with him, and he will bring joy to those who remain for thirty years.
“After these years, my son, the Messiah, will die, along with all who have human breath in them.
“The world will return to its original silence for seven days, as it was at the beginning, so that no one will remain.
“After seven days, the world that is now asleep will be awakened, and corruption will die.
“The earth will give up those who lie in it, the dust will give up those who sleep in it, and the storehouses will give up the souls deposited in them.
“The Most High will be revealed on the judgment seat, and the end will come. Mercy will pass away, compassion will depart, and patience will be withdrawn.
“My judgment alone will remain, truth will stand, and faithfulness will rejoice.
“Deeds will come forward, reward will be made known, righteous acts will awaken, and wicked acts will not sleep.
“The gulf of torment will appear, and opposite it the place of rest. The furnace of Gehenna will be revealed, and opposite it the paradise of delights.”
Then the Most High will say to those nations that are awakened, “Look and see what you have denied, whom you have not served, and whose commandments you have rejected.
Look, then, before you: here are rest and delights, and there are fire and torment.” He will say these things to them on that day of judgment.
For that day of judgment is like this: there is no sun in it, no moon, and no stars,
no clouds, no lightning, no thunder, no winds, no water, no air, no darkness, no evening, and no morning,
no summer, no winter, no beginning of the year, no heat, no ice, no frost, no hail, no dew, and no rain,
no noon, no night, no daytime, no light, no shining light, no brightness, and no radiance, but only the ray of the Most High’s glory, by which they will see what has been prepared.
Its duration will be like a week of years.
This is my judgment and its law, and I have made them known to you alone.
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, I said it then, and now I say it again: blessed are all those who have come and kept the commandments laid down by you.
But my petition concerns those others. For who among those who have come has not sinned? Or who among those born has not transgressed your commandment?
Now I see that the world to come is destined to bring delight to a few, but torment to many.

For there is an evil heart within us. It has led us astray from these things, brought us to destruction, shown us the ways of death, made known to us the paths of ruin, and driven us far from life. This has happened not to a few, but to nearly everyone who has ever lived.”
He answered and said to me, “Listen to me, Ezra, and I will tell you and instruct you again.
For this reason the Most High made not one world, but two.
As for your saying that the righteous are not many but few, listen to this in reply:
If you have precious stones, and they are few, set beside them an equal number of pieces of lead and clay.”
I said, “How is that possible, my lord?”
He answered and said to me, “Not only this: ask the earth, and it will tell you. Speak to it, and it will explain to you.
Say to it, ‘You have produced gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead, and clay.
But silver is more abundant than gold, bronze than silver, iron than bronze, lead than iron, and clay than lead.’
Compare them, then, and see: which are precious and valuable, the abundant things or the scarce ones?”
I answered and said, “Lord, my Lord, the abundant things are cheap, and the scarce ones are precious.”
He answered and said to me, “Then weigh within yourself what you have thought, because anyone who has only a small amount rejoices in it more than someone who has many things.
So it is with the promise of my judgment. For I rejoice and delight in the few who live, because they are the ones who now uphold my glory, and because of them my name has now been glorified.

I am not distressed over the multitude of those who perish. For they are the ones who have now become like vapor, who have been regarded as smoke and compared to a flame: they blazed up and went out.”
I answered and said, “O earth, what have you done, that these have been born from you and are going to destruction? But if understanding comes from dust, like the rest of created things,
it would have been better if even the dust itself had not existed, so that understanding would not have come from it.
But now understanding grows with us, and because of this we are tormented, because we perish knowingly.
Let the families of humanity mourn, but let the wild animals rejoice. Let all who are born lament, but let the cattle and sheep enjoy themselves.
For they are far better off than we are, because they do not await judgment or know torment, nor have they been promised life after death.
For what do we gain by being alive, except that we suffer torment?
For all who are born are entangled in sins and full of wrongdoing, and their downfalls weigh heavily upon them.
If we did not come to judgment after death, it would have been far better for us.”
He answered and said to me, “When the Most High was making the world, he prepared judgment beforehand for Adam and all who came from him, together with everything belonging to that judgment.
Now understand from your own words, for you said that understanding grows with us.

The inhabitants of the earth are therefore tormented for this reason: although they had understanding, they did wrong. They received commandments but did not keep them, and they also rejected the law that was established for them.
What, then, would they have to say at the judgment? Or how will they open their mouths and speak at the last time?
For how long the Most High has been patient with the inhabitants of the world! Yet it was not for their own sake, but because of the appointed times.”

I answered and said, “If I have found mercy in your sight, O Lord, my Lord, make this also known to your servant: after death, when each of us gives up our soul, are we kept at rest until those times arrive when you are to renew your creation, or are we tormented immediately?”
He answered and said to me, “I will tell you about this too. But do not associate yourself with the rebellious or count yourself among those who are tormented.
For you have a treasure of deeds stored with the Most High, and it will not be shown to you until the last times.

Now this is the account concerning death: when the final decree of judgment goes out from the Most High that a person must die, and the spirit separates from the body to be sent to the one who gave it, it first bows before the glory of God.
But if it belongs to the wrongdoers, or to those who did not keep the ways of the Most High, or to those who hated the people who fear God,
these souls do not enter the storehouses. Instead, they are immediately in torment, groaning and suffering in seven ways.
The first way: because they rebelled against the law of the Most High.
The second way: because they cannot return and do good deeds through which they might live.
The third way: because they see the reward stored up for those who believed.

The fourth way: when they know and understand the torment that awaits them at the end, to which the souls of the wicked are destined, because, when they had time to serve, they did not submit to the commandments of the Most High.
The fifth way: because they see the storehouses of the other souls, which are guarded by angels in great rest.
The sixth way: because they see the torment already prepared for them.

The seventh way, which is greater than all the ways mentioned before: they waste away in shame and are consumed by disgrace. They burn with fear as they see the glory of the Most High, before whom they sinned during their lives and before whom they are destined to be judged at the end.
But for those who have kept the way of the Most High, this is the way when the day comes for them to be freed from this perishable vessel.
For during the time they lived in it, they served the Most High with toil and endured danger at all times, because they fully kept the law of the one who laid down a law for them.
Therefore, this is the pronouncement concerning them.
First, they see with great joy the glory of the Most High, who has guided them. They find rest and come to it in seven ways.
The first way: because with great toil they struggled to overcome the evil thought that was formed within them, so that they would not stray from life into death.
The second way: they see the condition in which the souls of the wicked are tossed about and tormented, and the punishment reserved for them.
The third way: they see the testimony that their Creator bears about them, because during their lives they kept the law entrusted to them.
The fourth way: they see and understand their present rest—how, once gathered into their storehouses, they rest in great peace and are guarded by angels—and the glory reserved for them at the end.

The fifth way: they rejoice at how they have now escaped what is perishable and how they will inherit what is to come. They also see the distress and the great toil from which they have been freed, the relief they are destined to receive, and the delights they will enjoy as they become immortal.
The sixth way: when they are shown how their faces are destined to shine like the sun, and how they are destined to resemble the light of the stars and never decay again.

The seventh way, which is greater than all those mentioned before: they glory openly, take courage, and feel no shame. They eagerly hasten to see the face of the one whom they served during their lives, the one by whom they are destined to be glorified and from whom they will receive a reward.

These are the ways that the souls of the righteous can expect from now on. But the rebellious will receive from now on the ways of punishment mentioned before. These souls do not enter the storehouses, but from now on they are tormented with punishment, sighing and mourning in seven ways.
I answered and said, “Then will souls be given a place or a period of time after they are freed from their bodies, so that they may see what you have told me?”
He answered and said to me, “They have seven days of freedom. During those seven days they see these things mentioned before, and afterward they will be gathered into their storehouses.”

I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, tell me, your servant, this as well: whether on the day of judgment the righteous can plead for the wicked or petition the Most High on their behalf—

or fathers on behalf of their children, or children on behalf of their fathers, or brothers on behalf of their brothers, or relatives on behalf of their relatives, or friends on behalf of their friends.”

He answered and said to me, “Because you have found favor in my eyes, I will tell you about this as well. The day of judgment is a decisive day, and it reveals the seal of truth to everyone. For just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his servant, or a friend his loved one, to be sick in his place, or to sleep, or to eat, or to be healed,

so then, too, no one will be able to petition on another person’s behalf on that day, nor will anyone be able to place a burden on another. For then everyone will bear their own righteousness or wrongdoing.”
I answered and said, “But how is it, my lord, that we find that Abraham pleaded long ago for the people of Sodom, and Moses in the wilderness for our ancestors when they sinned,
and Joshua son of Nun after him for Israel in the days of Achan,
and Samuel in the days of Saul, and David over the calamity that struck the people, and Solomon for those in the sanctuary,
and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead man so that he might live,
and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many others on behalf of many?
If, then, even now, when corruption has become great and injustice has increased, the righteous have pleaded for the wicked, why, my lord, should it not be so then as well?”
He answered me, “This world has an end, and the glory of God does not remain in it forever. For this reason the strong have prayed for those who have no strength.”
But the day of judgment is the end of this world and the beginning of the world to come, which does not die and in which corruption passes away.
Licentiousness is dissolved, unbelief is abolished, righteousness grows, and truth dawns.
Then, therefore, no one can have mercy on someone condemned in judgment, nor harm someone acquitted in judgment.
I answered, “This is my first and last word: it would have been better for the earth not to have given birth to Adam, or, when it did give birth to him, to have instructed him not to sin.
For what benefit is there for all those who have come into existence? Look, we live in distress, and when we die we await torment.
Oh, what have you done, Adam? Although you sinned, the evil was not yours alone, but also ours, who have come from you.
For what benefit is there in this: an undying age has been promised to us, but we have done deeds that bring death?
And an unfailing hope has been made known to us, but we have wickedly been emptied of it?
And treasures free from anxiety and sickness are kept safe, but we ourselves have behaved wickedly?
And the glory of the Most High is to overshadow those who have lived chastely, but we have walked in evil ways?
And paradise is revealed, whose fruits do not decay, and in which there are delights and healing?
But we do not enter, because we have labored in evil places.
And the faces of the holy are to shine brighter than the stars, but our faces will become darker than darkness?
For during our lives, while we were acting unjustly, we did not consider that we would suffer after our death.”
And he answered me, “This is the meaning of the struggle fought on earth by a human being who is born.”
“If he is condemned, he will suffer what you have reckoned; but if he is acquitted, he will receive what you have said.

For this is the way of which Moses spoke to the people while he was alive. He said to them, ‘Look, today I have set before you life and death, good things and evil things. Therefore choose life for yourselves, so that you and your descendants may live.’
But they rebelled and did not obey him, or the prophets after him, or even me, who spoke with them.
For this reason, there should not be grief over their destruction as there is joy over the lives of those who obeyed.”
And I answered him, “I know, my lord, that the Most High is now called merciful because he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world.”
And gracious, because he shows grace to those who turn to his law;
And patient, because he is patient with us who sin, because we are what he has made;
And generous, because he desires to give rather than to demand;
And abundant in mercy, because he greatly increases his mercy toward those who exist now, those who have passed away, and those who are yet to come.
For if he did not increase his mercies, the world and its inhabitants could not live.
And generous, because unless he gave in his goodness so that wrongdoers might be relieved of their wrongdoing, not one in ten thousand human beings could live.
And judge, because unless he [?] those who were created by his word and forgot their many wrongdoings, only a very few would remain out of an innumerable multitude.
He answered and said to me, “The Most High made this world for many, but the world to come for few.

I will explain the matter to you, Ezra. It is as though you were to ask the earth, and it would tell you which soil it yields in greater quantity: that from which clay is made, or that from which gold is made. So it is with the making of this world.
Many have been created, but few will live.”
I answered and said, “Drink in knowledge, my soul, and drink understanding, my heart.
For you came unwillingly, and you depart against your will. Authority has not been given to you, except over a life of short duration.”

“O Lord, my Lord, if you permit your servant, I will plead before you. Give us seed and the cultivation of a new heart, from which fruit may come, so that every perishable being who has put on human form may be able to live.
For you are one, and we are one thing you have formed, the work of your hands, as you have said.

You give us life now in the womb, giving life to the body you have formed and putting its limbs together. Your creation is preserved in fire and water, and for nine months the body you formed bears the creature you created within it.
Both the one that guards and the one that is guarded are preserved by your own protection. And when the womb gives back what came into being within it,
you commanded milk to come from the limbs themselves, the fruit of full breasts.
So that what has been formed may grow for a little while, and afterward you guide it in your mercy.
You nourish him in your righteousness, guide him by your law, and instruct him in your wisdom.
You put him to death as your creation, and you give him life as your handiwork.
If, then, you quickly and easily destroy this being who was formed at your command with all this great labor, why, then, did he come into being?
What I have now said concerns everyone, but you know that I am especially troubled about your people,
and about your inheritance, over which I mourn, and about Israel, over whom I grieve, and about Jacob’s descendants, over whom I am distressed.
Therefore I will begin to plead and implore you on my own behalf and theirs, because I see the failings of those who live in the world.
But now I have also heard the sentence of the coming judgment.
Therefore hear my voice and listen to the words of my prayer, and I will speak before you, Lord my God.
Lord, you who dwell forever, whose heights are exalted and whose dwellings are in the air,
whose throne is without limit and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the heavenly armies stand in fear,
at whose word they are changed into fire and wind, whose word is trustworthy and whose utterance endures,
whose command is firm and whose pronouncements are fearsome, whose appearance dries up the deep and whose rebuke wipes away mountains, whose truth bears witness:
hear the voice of your servant, listen to the plea of the one you formed, and consider my words.
For while I am alive I will speak, and while I still have understanding I will give an answer.
Do not look at the failings of your people, but at those who have served you in truth.
Do not look at the follies of the wicked and their schemes, but at those who kept your covenants amid disgrace.
Do not consider those who behaved wickedly before you, but remember those who willingly learned to fear you.
Do not wish to destroy those who have become like cattle, but look at those who have received the light of your law.
Do not be angry with those who have behaved worse than wild animals, but love those who continually trusted in your glory.
For we and those before us have done destructive deeds and lived recklessly. But because of us sinners, you have been called merciful.
For if you choose to have mercy on us, who have no deeds, you are called gracious.
For the righteous, who have deeds stored up with you, have something to receive from their own deeds as their due.
For what is a human being that you should be angry with him, or a perishable race that you should be furious with it?
For truly, no one born has been free of wrongdoing, and no one who has lived has been free of sin.
For this is how your goodness is made known, Lord, my Lord: when you have mercy on those who have no strength of deeds.
He answered and said to me, “Some of these things you have spoken rightly, and it will be according to your words.
For truly, I do not concern myself with the creation of the wicked, or their death, or their judgment, or their destruction.
Rather, I delight in the coming into being of the righteous, in their lives, and in the payment of their reward.
For as you have spoken, so it will be.

For just as a farmer sows many seeds and plants many plants, yet not all the seeds survive in due season, nor do all the plants take root, so too not all those who have come into the world will live.”
I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, let me speak before you.
For if the farmer’s seed does not receive your rain at the proper time, can it live? Yet it is also ruined by too much rain.
But a human being, who was formed by your hands and made in your likeness, for whose sake you created everything—have you compared him to the farmer’s seed?
No! I beg you, Lord, my Lord, have pity on your people and have mercy on your inheritance, for it is on your own creatures that you are showing mercy.”
He answered and said to me, “The things of the present are for those who live now, and the things to come are for those who are to come.
For you fall far short of being able to love my creation more than I do. But you have made yourself very much like the wicked. Let it not be so.
But in this too you will be praised before the Most High,
because you humbled yourself as you ought and did not place yourself above the righteous. For this reason you will be praised all the more.
For the inhabitants of the world will suffer great misery at the end, in return for the great pride in which it boasted.
But you, consider yourself, and seek the glories of those who are like you.

For paradise has been opened for you, the tree of life has been planted, the world to come has been prepared, delight has been made ready, the city has been built, rest has been established, goodness has been perfected, and wisdom has been brought to completion.
The root has been sealed off from you, and disease has died out among you. Death has been hidden, Sheol has fled, and corruption has been forgotten.
Pains have been removed from you, and at the end the treasures of life have been revealed.
Therefore, do not ask any further about the many who perish.
For they received freedom and rejected the Most High. They also utterly despised his law and abandoned his ways.
They also trampled on his holy ones.
And they said in their hearts that there is no God, although they knew full well that they would die.
For this reason, just as these things foretold await you, so thirst and the coming torment await them. For the Most High does not wish human beings to perish.
But those who were created dishonored the name of their Maker, denied his grace, and did not acknowledge me, who prepared life for them.
For this reason my judgment has drawn near,
which I have not made known to many, but only to you and the few who are like you. And I answered and said:
“Now, Lord, you have made known to me many signs that you are going to perform in the last days, but you have not made known to me at what time.”
He answered and said to me, “Measure it carefully for yourself: when you see that one part of the signs foretold has passed,
then understand that this is the time when the Most High is going to visit the world that was made by him.
And when there appear in the world earthquakes in various regions, turmoil among the crowds, intrigue among the nations, disturbances among rulers, and panic among leaders—
Then it became clear that the Most High had spoken about these things long ago.
for just as everything that happens in the world has a known beginning and an evident end,
so also are the times of the Most High: their beginnings are known through indications, signs, and mighty deeds, and their endings through punishment and signs.
And everyone who survives, everyone who is able to escape through his deeds or through the faith with which he has believed,
will be spared the danger foretold and will see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I set apart for myself from of old.
Then those who now neglect my ways will be astonished, and those who despised and rejected them will be in torment.
For all those who did not acknowledge me during their lives, while I was doing good to them,
and all those who acted arrogantly against my law, who had freedom,
and who, while an opportunity for patience lay open to them, did not understand but were negligent—these must come to know after death.
Therefore, from now on do not inquire how the wicked are tormented, but ask how the righteous will live, those to whom the world belongs and for whose sake the world came into being.”
And I answered and said:
“Even now I say again, and afterward I will say again, that those who perish are more numerous than those who live,
just as the waves are greater than a little drop.”
He answered and said to me, “As the land is, so are its seeds; as the flowers are, so are their colors; as the craftsman is, so are the perfumes; and as the farmer is, so is the threshing floor.”
For it was in the time of the world, when I was preparing those who now exist, before the worlds came into being, so that they might live in it. No one stood against me, for there was no one at all.
But now that they have been created in a well-ordered world, with a table that lacks nothing and a law beyond searching out, they have corrupted themselves by their deeds.
I looked at my world, and there it was, ruined; at my inhabited earth, and there it was, in danger because of the conduct of its inhabitants.
I looked and had pity on a very few, and I kept alive for myself one grape from a cluster and one plant from a great forest.
So let the multitude perish, because it has become worthless. But let my grape and my plant be preserved, for they were produced with great labor.
But as for you, if you set yourself apart for another seven days, do not fast during them again.
Go to the plain of flowers, where no house has been built, and eat only the flowers of the plain. Taste no meat and drink no wine, but eat only flowers.
Seek the Most High earnestly, and I will come to you and speak with you.
I went, as he commanded me, to the plain called Arpad and sat there among the flowers of the earth. I ate the roots of the open country, and eating them satisfied me.
After seven days, as I was lying on the grass, my heart began to be troubled within me again, as before.
My mouth opened, and I began to speak before the Most High. I said:

O Lord, my Lord, you revealed yourself to our ancestors in the wilderness of Sinai when they had come out of Egypt and were passing through the wilderness, through a land bearing no fruit, where no one had passed. You said to them:
You, Israel, listen to me; descendants of Jacob, pay attention to my words.
For look, I am sowing my law in you, and it will produce the fruits of righteousness among you, and you will glory in it forever.
Our ancestors received the law but did not keep it, and the commandments but did not carry them out. Yet they had the imperishable fruits of your law, for these could not perish, because it is yours.
But those who received it perished because they did not keep what had been sown in them.
And this is the rule: when the earth receives seed, or the sea a ship, or any other container in which food is placed, or anything that has been deposited, or anything that has been stored—
these things perish, but those that received them remain. With us, however, it was not so.
Rather, we who received the law and sinned perish along with our heart, which received it.
But your law does not perish; it endures in its glory.

While I was saying these things in my heart, I raised my eyes and saw a woman on the right, tossing about and weeping loudly. She was sighing within herself and was deeply distressed. Her clothes were torn, and dust lay on her head.
I left the thoughts I had been thinking, turned toward her, and said to her:
Why are you weeping and so distressed within yourself?
She answered me, “Leave me alone, my lord, so that I may weep over myself and continue to sigh, for my soul is deeply embittered, and I am utterly brought low.”
I said to her, “Tell me what has happened to you.” She answered me:
I, your servant, was barren and bore no children, though I had lived with my husband for thirty years.
But every day and every hour throughout those thirty years, I prayed and pleaded with the Most High, by day and by night.

After those thirty years, God heard the voice of your servant, saw her humiliation, looked upon my suffering, and gave me a son. My husband and I, and all the people of my city, rejoiced and took great delight in him, and we praised the Mighty One.
I raised him with great toil.
When he grew up, I set about finding him a wife, and I held a day of feasting and great celebration.
But when my son entered his bridal chamber, he fell down and died.
I overturned the lamps, and all the people of my city came forward to comfort me. I remained quiet until the next day and until nightfall.
After they had all fallen asleep, thinking that I too was asleep, I got up in the night and fled. I came to this plain, as you now see.
I intend never to enter the city again, but to remain here. I will neither eat nor drink, but will continually mourn and fast until I die.
Then I put aside the thoughts I had been thinking, and answered her angrily:
You are more foolish than all other women! Do you not see our mourning and what has happened to us?
Look, Zion, the mother of us all, is in great distress and has been deeply humiliated.
Now mourning is called for, and we are all mourning. You grieve over one son, but we—the whole world—grieve over our mother.
Ask the earth, and she will tell you that she ought to mourn, because so many have lived upon her.
From the beginning, all who have lived upon her, and the others who are still to come—look, they all go to destruction, and their multitude comes to ruin.
Who, then, ought to mourn more: she who has lost this entire multitude, or you who mourn for one?
But if you say to me, ‘My mourning is not like the earth’s, because I have lost the fruit of my womb, whom I bore in labor and raised with pain.’
‘As for the earth, the multitude that came to her has passed away just as it came, in accordance with the earth’s nature.’ But I say to you again:
Just as you gave birth with toil, so too the earth, from the beginning, has given her fruit—humanity—to her Maker.
Now, then, contain your grief within yourself, and bear with strength the misfortune that has happened to you.
For if you acknowledge the justice of the Most High’s judgment, you will also receive your son back in time, and you will be praised among women.
“Go, then, into the city to your husband.” And she answered me:
I will not do that, and I will not enter the city or return to my husband. Instead, I will die here.
I spoke to her again and said:
No, woman, no! Do not do this. Instead, let Zion’s suffering persuade you, and take comfort because of Jerusalem’s pain.
For you have seen our sanctuaries laid waste, our altars overturned, and our temple demolished.

Our worship has ceased, our songs of praise have been taken away, our glory has fallen, the light of our lampstand has gone out, the ark of the covenant has been seized, our holy things have been defiled, and the name by which we are called has been profaned. Our freeborn people have been dishonored, our priests have been burned in the fire, our Levites have been taken captive, our virgins have been defiled, our women have been violated by force, our seers have been seized, our righteous people have been scattered, our young men have been enslaved, and our mighty men have been weakened.
And greater than all these is what has happened to the seal of Zion: the seal of her glory has now been taken away, and she has been handed over to those who hate us.
You, therefore, cast off your many sorrows, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you and the Most High may relieve you of the pains of your weariness.

While I was speaking with her, her face suddenly shone very brightly, and the appearance of her face became like lightning. I was very afraid to approach her, and my heart was utterly astonished. While I was wondering what this vision meant,
she suddenly cried out in a loud and terrifying voice, so that the whole earth shook at her voice.
And I looked, and behold, I no longer saw a woman, but a city being built. The place appeared as though on great foundations. I was afraid and cried out in a loud voice and said:
Where is the angel Uriel, who came to me on the first day? For he has brought me into this great turmoil. My end has become destruction, and my prayer a disgrace.
While I was still saying these things, lying on the ground like a dead man, the angel who had come to me before came to me and saw me
lying on the ground like a dead man, with my mind bewildered. He took me by my right hand, strengthened me, and set me on my feet. He said to me,
“What is wrong with you? Why are you trembling? Why have your thoughts and the understanding of your heart become confused?” And I said to him,
“Because you abandoned me. For I did as you told me and went out to the plain. And now I have seen, and am still seeing, something I cannot explain.” He answered and said to me,
“Stand on your feet, and I will explain it to you.” And I said to him,
“Speak, my lord. Only do not abandon me, so that I do not die before my time.
For I have seen something I did not know, and I am hearing something I do not understand.
Or perhaps my mind is deceiving me, and my soul is seeing a dream.
But now I ask you, my lord: explain this terrifying vision to your servant.”
He answered and said to me, “Listen to me, and I will teach you. I will explain to you the things you fear, for the Most High has revealed many mysteries to you.
For he has seen your uprightness: you are deeply distressed over your people, you mourn greatly over your people, and you mourn greatly over Zion.
This, then, is the meaning: that woman who appeared to you a little while ago,
who was mourning, and whom you began to comfort,
now no longer appears to you as a woman, but has appeared to you as a city being built.
And as for what she was telling you about her son’s misfortune, this is the explanation:
The woman you saw is Zion, which you now see as a city being built.
And when she told you that she had been barren for thirty years, it was because she had existed in the world for three thousand years without any sacrifice being offered in her.
After three thousand years, Solomon built the city and offered sacrifice in her. It was then that the barren woman gave birth to a son.
And when she told you that she had raised him in the world, this was the time when Jerusalem was inhabited.
And when she told you, ‘My son entered his bridal chamber and died,’ this is the downfall and calamity of Jerusalem.
And when you saw her likeness, how she mourned for her children, you began to comfort her over what had happened to her.
And now the Most High has seen that you are distressed with all your soul and that your whole heart aches for her, and he has shown you the light of her glory and the beauty of her splendor.
For this reason I told you to wait for me in the plain, where no house had been built.
For I knew that the Most High was going to show you all these things.
For this reason I told you to come to a place where there is no foundation of a building.
For no human work could remain in the place where the city of the Most High was to be revealed.
But do not be afraid, and do not let your heart be shaken. Instead, enter and see the light of her glory and the greatness of her buildings, as much as your eyes are able to see.
And after this you will hear as much as your ears are able to hear.
For you have been blessed more than many, and you have been named before the Most High among the few.
But tomorrow night you are to remain here.
And the Most High will show you a vision of revelations concerning what the Most High will do to the inhabitants of the earth in the last days.
And I slept there another night, as he had commanded me.
And on the second night I saw a vision: an exceedingly large eagle was rising from the sea. It had twelve wings and three heads.
And I looked, and it spread its wings over the whole earth. All the winds of heaven were blowing toward it, and the clouds were gathering toward it.
And I saw thin, slender, small wings growing out of its wings.
Its heads, however, were at rest. The middle head was larger than the others, but it too was at rest with them.
And I looked, and the eagle commanded its wings to rule over the whole earth and its inhabitants.
And I saw how everything under heaven was subject to it, and none of the creatures on earth resisted it.
And I looked, and the eagle stood on its talons and called out to its wings, saying to them, “Go and rule over the whole earth. But now be at rest.”
“Do not seek to wake up all together. Instead, sleep, each of you in its own place, and wake up in turn.”
“But let the heads be kept for the end.”
And I saw that its voice did not come from its heads, but from the middle of its body.
And I counted its small wings, and there were eight of them.
And I looked, and one wing rose up on the right side and ruled over the whole earth.
And I saw that its end came and it perished, so that not even its place could be known. And I looked, and a second wing rose up, and it too ruled over the whole earth for a long time.
And after it had ruled, its end came, and it was destroyed like the first.
And a voice was heard speaking to it:
“Listen, you who have held the earth all this time. Expect this before you are destroyed:
None of those who come after you will hold it for so long, not even for half that time.”
And I looked, and the third wing rose and ruled over the whole earth, just as its former companions had. It too was destroyed like the former ones.
And this happened to all the wings: each of them ruled in turn and then was destroyed.
And I looked, and after a time the small wings also rose on the right side to take possession of the earth. Some of them held it, but they were quickly destroyed.
Some of them rose but did not gain power.
And I looked after these things, and its twelve wings had been destroyed, along with two of the small wings.
Nothing remained of the eagle’s body except its three heads, which were resting, and six small wings.
And I looked, and two wings separated from among the small wings and went and stood beneath the head on the right side. But four remained in their place.
And I looked, and those four small wings were planning to rise and take power.
And I looked, and one rose, but it was quickly destroyed.
Then a second rose, but it too was destroyed, even more quickly than the first.
And I looked, and the two of them that remained were themselves also planning to take leadership.
While they were planning to rule over the earth, I looked, and one of the heads that had been resting—the middle one—awoke. It was larger than the other two heads.
[?] the two of them with it.
And it turned, together with the two that were with it, and devoured both of those small wings that were planning to rule.
That head took possession of the whole earth and subjected its inhabitants to great hardship. It exercised greater power over the world than all the wings that had come before.
And I looked after these things, and suddenly that middle head was also destroyed, just as the wings had been.
But two heads remained, and they too ruled over the whole earth and its inhabitants.
And I looked, and the head on the right side devoured the one on the left.
And I heard a voice saying to me, “Look ahead of you, Ezra, and see what outcome you see.”
And I looked, and there was something like a lion roused from the forest, crying out and roaring. And I heard it utter a human voice toward the eagle, speaking and saying to it:
“Listen, eagle, and I will speak to you. The Most High says to you:”
Are you not the one that remained of these four beasts, which I had made to rule over my world, and through which the end of the times was to come?

But you came fourth and defeated all the beasts that had gone before. You gained power over the world through great suffering, and over the whole earth through bitter oppression. Through deceit you inhabited the earth for a long time.
And you judged the earth unjustly.

For you plundered and robbed the meek and the faithful. You harmed the humble, hated the upright, and loved liars. You demolished the fortresses of those who prospered and brought down the walls of those who had not harmed you.
Your insolence rose up to the Most High, to the Mighty One.
The Most High looked at his times, and behold, they were complete, and his ages had reached their fulfillment.
Therefore you will certainly be destroyed, you eagle, along with your lofty wings, your small and evil wings, your cruel heads, your evil talons, and your whole hateful and evil body.
So that the whole earth may find rest and relief. But when it has been delivered from oppression, it awaits the judgment and mercy of its Maker.
While the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked.
And behold, the head that remained was suddenly destroyed. Then those two wings that had gone over to it rose up to rule. Their rule would come to an end and would be full of turmoil.
And I saw that they too were destroyed, and the eagle’s whole body was burning. The earth was greatly astonished. But I awoke because of the intense trembling and great fear, and I said to myself:
For you have done all these things to me because you investigate the ways of the Most High.
And now I am weakened in my soul, and my spirit has greatly failed. Not even a little strength remains in me because of the great terror that frightened me this night.
And now I will ask the Most High to strengthen me to the end.
And I said, “O Lord, my Lord, if I have found mercy in your eyes, and if I truly have greater favor with you than many others, and if my prayer has truly risen before your majestic presence,
strengthen me and make known to me, your servant, the explanation and interpretation of this vision that I have seen, so that you may fully comfort my soul.
For it was not because I am worthy that you chose me to reveal to me the end of the times and the conclusion of the seasons.” And he answered and said to me,
“This is the interpretation of the vision that you saw.
The eagle that you saw rising from the sea is the fourth kingdom, which appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel.
But it was not explained to him as I am explaining it to you now, or as I have explained it to you.
Behold, the days are coming when a kingdom will arise on the earth, and it will be more terrifying than all the kingdoms that came before it.
Twelve kings will reign in it, one after another.
But when the second reigns, he will hold power longer than those twelve.
This is the interpretation of the twelve wings that you saw.
And as for your seeing a voice speaking, which came not from the eagle’s head but from the middle of its body:
This is its meaning. During the time of that kingdom there will be many divisions, and it will be in danger of falling. Yet it will not fall then, but will be restored to its former rule.
And as for your seeing eight small wings that grew beneath its wings:
This is its meaning. Eight kings will arise in it, whose times will be short and whose seasons will pass quickly. Two of them will perish.
When the time comes to divide it. And four will be kept for a time, so that when its time comes, it may end. But two will be kept for the end.
And as for your seeing three heads on it that were at rest:
This is the meaning: At the end of the times, the Most High will raise up three kings. They will introduce many changes in it and crush the earth.
And its inhabitants with great hardship, more than all those who came before them. For this reason they were called the eagle’s heads.
For they are the ones who renew its wickedness, and they will bring it to its end.
And as for your seeing that one great head destroyed: It is because one of them alone will die on his bed, though he too will suffer torment.
But the sword will devour the two who remain.
For the sword of one will devour his companion, but he too will fall by the sword in the end.
And because you saw two wings go to the head on the right side:
This is the meaning: These are the ones whom the Most High has set apart for its end. Their kingdom will come to an end, and it will be filled with turmoil.
As you saw. And as for your seeing a lion roused from the thicket, crying out and roaring and speaking to the eagle, rebuking it for its injustice, with all the words that you heard:

He is the Messiah, whom the Most High has kept for the end of days, who will arise from the offspring of David. He will come and speak with them, rebuke them for their wickedness, reprimand them for their wrongdoing, and lay their injustice before them.
For he will bring them alive before me for their judgment. And after he has rebuked them, he will destroy them.

But he will mercifully rescue the remnant of my people, those who have remained within my borders. He will give them joy until the end of the day of judgment comes, about which I spoke with you before.
This is the vision you saw, and this is its interpretation.
You alone have been found worthy to know the mystery of the Most High.
Therefore write in a book all these things that you have seen, and put them in a hidden place.
Teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to hold fast and keep these mysteries.
But you must wait here another seven days, so that whatever the Most High wishes to reveal to you may be revealed to you.

Then he went away from me. And when the people saw that seven days had passed and I had not come into the city, all the people gathered, from the least to the greatest. They got up and came to me, and said to me:
How have we sinned against you, or what harm have we done you, that you have left us and settled here?
For you alone are left to us out of all the prophets, like a cluster of grapes left from the harvest, like a lamp in a dark place, and like a safe harbor for a ship caught in a storm.
Are the calamities that have befallen us not enough for us, that you too should leave us?
If you are leaving us, it would have been better for us if we too had burned when Zion burned.
For we are no better than those who died there. And I wept in a loud voice, and I answered and said to them:
Take courage, Israel, and do not grieve, house of Jacob.
For you are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One will never forget you.
I have not left you, nor am I leaving you. Rather, I came to this place to plead concerning the devastation of Zion and to ask for mercy over the humiliation of our sanctuary.
And now, go, everyone to his own home. I will come to you after these days.
The people went to the city, as I had told them.
But I stayed in the plain for seven days, as he had commanded me. I ate only wildflowers, and roots were my food during those days.
After seven days, I saw a vision in the night.
And look, a great wind arose in the sea, stirring up all its waves.

And I looked, and behold, that wind brought up from the heart of the sea something resembling a human being. And I looked, and behold, that man was flying with the clouds of heaven. Wherever he turned his face to look and see, everything trembled before his gaze.
Wherever the sound from his mouth reached, everyone who heard his voice melted, as wax melts when fire touches it.
After this I looked, and there was an innumerable multitude of people gathered from the four winds of heaven to fight against the man who had come up from the sea.
I saw that he cut out a high mountain for himself, flew up, and stood on it.
I tried to see the region or place from which that mountain had been cut out, but I could not.
After this I looked, and all those who had gathered to fight against him were very afraid. Nevertheless, they dared to fight.
When he saw the onrush of the approaching multitude, he did not raise his hand. He was not holding a spear or any weapon of war. But I saw

how he sent out from his mouth alone what looked like waves of fire, and from his lips a flaming wind. From his tongue he hurled coals in a whirlwind. All these mingled together: the waves of fire, the flaming wind, and the mass of the whirlwind.

They fell upon the onrush of that great multitude, which was ready to fight, and burned them all up so suddenly that nothing could be seen of that innumerable crowd except ash dust and the smell of smoke. I saw this and was amazed.
After this, I saw that man come down from the mountain and call to himself another great crowd, a peaceful one.

Many human figures approached him. Some were rejoicing, some were sorrowful, some were bound, and some were bringing others who were approaching. I awoke, trembling violently, and prayed to the Most High, saying:
You are the one who from the beginning showed your servant these wonders. Although I am unworthy, you thought fit to accept my petition.
Now reveal to me also the interpretation of this vision.
For as I consider it in my mind, woe to those who survive in those days, and much greater woe to those who do not survive!
For because they did not survive, they will be distressed
over what is reserved for those who survive in the last days, while they themselves do not attain it. And for those who survive too,
there is woe for this reason: they see great dangers and many afflictions, as these visions show.
Nevertheless, it is better for someone to face danger and reach these things than to pass from the world like a cloud and not see what happens at the end of the ages.
And he answered and said to me, “I will also tell you the interpretation of your vision, and I will reveal to you the things you spoke about.”
